task: Expose exported object method signatures from canonical ABI-v10 records without relying on legacy semantic rows.
observation: The ABI-v10 nominal-template writer discarded the entire exported object template when one method had a non-no-op body, even when that method was a pure constant return whose callable signature and zero observable effects were straightforward to prove.
impact: ABI-v10 method templates now cover proven pure primitive literals, typed unused READ parameters, and a single unchanged typed parameter returned from a method. The source-free tests preserve Vector[Int] CONSUME and a three-parameter selection where only the returned String is CONSUME; later reuse of either consumed argument is rejected. The regression now also removes the legacy type:Point, enum, and domain binary rows, proving the canonical nominal and method-template records supply the declaration and all eight signatures.
evidence: java -cp compiler-java/bin:compiler-java/lib/* org.mosslang.compiler.cli.Main effects method:Point.select_right --source tmp/source-free-method-select.moss --json
MOSS_STAGED_ABI=v10 ./scripts/java/test.sh (with legacy type:Point, enum, and domain records stripped)

resolution.summary: Pure literal-return and unchanged typed-parameter method signatures with checked READ/CONSUME modes are serialized and consumed without legacy semantic rows. The source-free ownership tests and focused C++/Java query for multi-parameter access modes agree; all eleven Java tests pass in both ABI modes. General method bodies/effects, generic relations, and native linkage remain incomplete. The strengthened consumer removes legacy nominal/type, enum, domain, and semantic rows before loading the point template.

task: Protect ABI-v10 method receiver CONSUME through source-free template encode/load and semantic call checking.
observation: The source-free object fixture tested WRITE receiver restoration and parameter CONSUME, but did not exercise a method template whose receiver itself was CONSUME.
impact: The focused test now encodes and imports a CONSUME receiver mode and confirms a consumer's later use is rejected. This records source-free metadata and ownership call-site behavior without claiming native linkage parity.

resolution.summary: Source-free ABI-v10 receiver CONSUME survives encode/load and rejects caller reuse; native linkage remains a final acceptance gate.

task: Verify imported source-free method CONSUME propagates through a local helper function.
observation: Source-free Point.replace declares its Vector argument CONSUME. A local forward helper calling replace propagates that mode to its own parameter, and a caller cannot return the Vector after forwarding it.
impact: The focused regression confirms ABI-loaded method access metadata participates in local function summary closure and caller ownership checks.

resolution.summary: Source-free method CONSUME propagates through a local helper and rejects caller reuse; all eleven Java test classes pass in ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Native linkage remains a final acceptance gate.

task: Preserve source-free ABI-v9 typed raise variants for imported functions and methods.
observation: Source-free imported ABI-v9 functions and object methods with raise_set=enum:Fault:Bad had no body for Java to inspect, so unhandled calls from main were accepted.
impact: Java now retains enum variants from source-free function and method metadata and includes them in root raise closure. Focused consumers reject unhandled calls and accept exact recover arms.

resolution.summary: Imported ABI-v9 typed raises from functions and object methods now reject unhandled main escape and allow exact recovery; all eleven Java test classes pass under ABI-v9 and staged ABI-v10. Multi-variant encoding and source-free native execution remain open.
